NeuraWall · AI-assisted network security

A firewall that never blocks on its own.

Claude proposes the rule. You see what it would have blocked in your own traffic. A person approves it, and it rolls out in stages.

Start freeRead the docs

Free for one node. Sign in with your NEXORA account.

Watch. Propose. Approve.

Three tiers of inference raise the alert. Only a rule a person approved can ever block.

Watch

Statistics, machine learning and traffic classifiers read flow metadata. Nothing is decrypted, and payloads are never stored.

Propose

Claude triages the alert and drafts a narrow rule that starts alert-only. Without a Claude key, an offline advisor drafts it on your own host.

Approve and roll out

The draft is replayed against recent legitimate traffic first. A signed bundle goes to 5% of nodes, then 25%, then all, and rolls back if blocking jumps.

No black box

See the blast radius before you ship.

Every draft shows how much of your legitimate traffic it would have matched. Every drop maps to a rule id you approved. Models can raise an alert, never a block.

  • Replay against recent traffic before approval
  • Optional four-eyes: the author cannot approve their own rule
  • Downgrading a plan never changes what your nodes enforce

Questions, answered.

Does it decrypt my traffic?

No. It analyses metadata and never intercepts TLS. That is a design decision, not a missing feature.

Can the AI block my traffic by itself?

No. A model can only raise an alert or draft an alert-only rule. A person approves any rule that enforces.

What if Claude is unavailable, or I don't want to use it?

An offline advisor does the same jobs deterministically, and nothing leaves your host.

What happens if the control plane goes down?

Nodes keep enforcing their last signed bundle. The console being down does not change what nodes enforce.

What data does Claude see?

Flow metadata, passed as delimited untrusted data under a call budget. Every drafted rule is schema-checked, forced to alert-only and simulated before a person sees it.

Can I import my current rules?

Not yet.

Is it open source?

No. NeuraWall is proprietary software.
